transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, the central compressed-air dryer serving Lines 5 and 7 is due for desiccant replacement this week, and we have a portable compressor available for temporary service during the work. I need to run through our routine pre-shutdown review before I can finalize the work order. We'll go in order: quality first, then utilities, then production control, and finally environmental health and safety. Once I've heard from all four of you, I'll finalize the shutdown decision. Could quality please start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Maya, before we proceed, I need to flag a quality concern. My quality review found that Line 7's pneumatic process requires compressed air at a dew point of -40 degrees Celsius or lower. The portable compressor cannot meet that dew point limit. I recorded this requirement in today's quality notebook but have not yet attached it to the shutdown work order. We'll need to address this before finalizing the plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Maya, I have an important update for the utilities review. I confirmed with the dryer service technician this morning by email: the desiccant replacement requires 5 hours of isolation work followed by exactly 2 hours of pressure stabilization before production air can be released. This estimate has not yet been entered in the maintenance schedule, so we need to account for a total of 7 hours before Lines 5 and 7 can resume normal production air service.
